rubric.name: 像真人在讲
rubric.question: 逐句：自然 / 有点怪 / 很怪。书面腔、讲解腔、翻译腔、念稿感、报菜名式罗列都算怪

rubric.name: 衔接与过渡
rubric.question: 开场、本期内容、章节转换、举例前后：像一个人顺着思路往下讲，而不是「下面讲第一点」式的模板或目录朗读；上下句接得上

rubric.name: 一遍听懂
rubric.question: 只靠耳朵：一句只带一个新意思；指代清楚（说「这个」时观众知道指什么）；术语先解释再用；数字、同音字不会听错

rubric.name: 精炼
rubric.question: 没有废话、重复、正确的空话；删掉不影响理解的句子要指出来

rubric.name: 口吻与节奏
rubric.question: 从头到尾是同一个亲切、清楚、不端着的讲解者；长短句交替，每句适合一口气念完

rubric.name: Sounds like a person talking
rubric.question: Each line: natural / a bit off / clearly off. Written-style, lecture tone, translated-from-Chinese phrasing, telegraphic lists all count as off

rubric.name: Flow and transitions
rubric.question: Cold open, the 'what's coming' part, chapter changes, before/after examples: does it sound like one person following a thought, not 'Point one…' templates or a TOC read aloud? Do adjacent lines connect?

rubric.name: Clear on one hearing
rubric.question: Ear only: one new idea per line; clear reference ('this' points to something); terms explained before used; numbers and words not misheard

rubric.name: Tight
rubric.question: No filler, repetition, or empty truisms; point out lines that could go without losing anything

rubric.name: Voice and rhythm
rubric.question: One warm, clear, unpretentious narrator throughout; varied sentence length; each line sayable in one breath

rubric.name: Rewrites
rubric.question: For every 'a bit off' / 'clearly off' line, a drop-in rewrite no longer than the original; rank the 5 most awkward lines

V1.evidence: Most of the video sounds spoken ("Feel again, step again, and you get there", l11; "It never saw the whole map. It only felt the ground underfoot", l29). Written-style lines: l13 "Which way each knob should turn to drop the score fastest, all together, is the gradient"; l17 "the taxi data is illustrative"; l51 "lots of little knob-filled units in layers".

V2.evidence: The cold open (l01-l07) and the chapter flow are one person following a thought, with no TOC read aloud. Breaks: l17 "the taxi data" appears with no setup; l50 "a straight line with two knobs" comes from nowhere; l37 "The one in between" does not say which rate; l03 repeats l02.

V3.evidence: l20-l21 "The base fare drops the score one point seven ... Both should go up" is hard to parse on one hearing (what drops? what goes up?); l50 "a straight line" is never introduced; l17 "taxi data" is never introduced; l35 lists three numbers (ninety-six, a hundred eighteen, a hundred forty-five) in 2.7s; l12/l13 stack abstractions (slope = score change per nudge, gradient = direction for all knobs).

V5.evidence: One warm, plain narrator, with short punchy lines ("How does it find the bottom?", l06; "Five steps in, it's off the map", l36). Weak spots: l12 and l45 run long, so a breath is needed mid-line. l18 and l34 are dense with numbers.

items.checks: Screen by screen: is the on-screen English an outline (not prose), tight, divided from the narration, and readable in time?
items.how: Hard limits (report every breach): title ≤6 words; any other block ≤9 words; ≤4 text blocks per screen (not counting the small eyebrow label, source line or chart ticks); ≤22 words per screen. Narration subtitles also sit at the bottom of the frame. Counting rules (round-2 ruling, 2026-11-09): eyebrow labels, case tabs, source lines and end-card credits are exempt; a list, table or card row of look-alike items (each ≤6 words, at most 6 items) counts as one block, and numbering doesn't count as words; in-chart text (zone names, curve names, axis titles, bar labels, callouts) counts toward words and the whole chart counts as one block — only axis tick numbers are exempt; a table's column headers count with the table.
items.what: Screen by screen: is the on-screen English an outline (not prose), tight, divided from the narration, and readable in time?
items.problem: The previous version put full sentences on screen (e.g. 'A separate model identified the hospital for scans from two hospitals — a hospital fingerprint'), repeating the narration. The user wants outline-only, concise slides (2026-11-08).

rubric.name: Outline, not prose
rubric.question: Only keywords, short phrases, key numbers, labels; no full narration sentences. Count words per screen against the hard limits

rubric.name: Divided from narration
rubric.question: Screen carries structure, numbers, contrasts; narration explains. No verbatim repetition, no new claims the narration doesn't make; terms match the narration

rubric.name: Hierarchy and consistency
rubric.question: What reads first, second; ≤3 levels (title, point, note); numbering, labels, chapter names and agenda items consistent with each other

rubric.name: Native phrasing and style
rubric.question: Sentence case headline style; no Chinglish; consistent punctuation (no trailing periods on fragments), en dashes, quotes; parallel grammar in lists; **chapter titles and headings must read naturally aloud** — awkward noun stacks are must-fix

rubric.name: Readable in time
rubric.question: From the screenshot and how long it stays: readable in time (~3 words/s while also reading subtitles and the chart)

rubric.name: Rewrites
rubric.question: For every breach or awkward phrase, a shorter drop-in rewrite

P1.evidence: Hard limits broken on two screens. l20 (6.2s) carries about 23 counted words (chart 7 + knobs 6 + 78/0 + the two delta rows "Base fare +$0.10 −1.7" / "Per km +$0.10 −11.2" = 8). l38 carries 26 words (title 4 + three panel heads 9 + three result lines 13, including "Score" x3). Otherwise titles are all ≤6 words and blocks ≤9 words; most screens are real outlines (l11 "Feel, step, repeat", l46 table). Outro card is sentence-like.

P2.evidence: Division of labour is mostly good (numbers, contrasts, labels on screen). Near-verbatim echoes: l24 "The floor: a long, gentle trench" vs narration "The floor is a long, gentle trench"; l47 "Turned one small step at a time" vs "one small step at a time"; l45 "Each knob gets its own step size" vs "gives each knob its own step size"; outro "Feel for the steepest way down" is l48 word for word. l04 "Billions: no map" understates "hundreds of billions of knobs".

P3.evidence: Chapter numbering 01–04 and eyebrows are consistent, and ≤3 levels hold. But the defined terms "The gradient" (l13) and "The learning rate" (l15) appear only as a 22px eyebrow while a paraphrase is the h1 ("Fastest way down", "How big each step"), so the term being taught reads last. l40 "Upgrade ①/②" circled numerals clash with "01–04" chapter numbering. "Score" caption is repeated three times in l34–l38.

P4.evidence: Strict items. Chapter title "How big models train" garden-paths (reads as "how big models..."). Chapter card "Downhill, blindfolded" is a fragment, not a natural spoken title. Cold open l04 "Billions: no map" lacks its noun and l01 "Lower is better" vs l02 "Lowest = best" mixes "is" and "=". Outro lines are not parallel ("Feel for the steepest way down" is an imperative; "Step size is the learning rate" is a sentence). l23 "Into the valley in 3" is clipped ("3" what?). l30 "What if it's wrong?" has no antecedent on screen. l40 "A small batch per step" / "Smarter steps" not parallel.

P5.evidence: Screens in s2 and s0 are light and readable (l09–l11 at 6 words in 3 to 6s). Overloaded: l20 (23 words in 6.2s plus chart), l38 (26 words in 5.4s; most of it persists from l36/l37, so only the title is new). Subtitles sit at the bottom, and l37/l38 panels end at about y=880 of 1080, which is tight. Chapter-card and outro screenshots are not provided, so their timing is unchecked.

P6.evidence: Every row in the issue table has a drop-in rewrite, checked against the word limits (for example l38 rewrite totals 22 words; l20 rewrite totals 19).

P1.evidence: l20–l21 contain 23 counted words after restoring chart text; l38–l39 contain 26 even excluding step numbering. l45 retains a complete explanatory sentence.

P2.evidence: l33–l39 add “Still halfway,” whereas narration says “still far from the bottom.” l45 and the outro repeat explanations already delivered aloud.

P3.evidence: The four supplied chapter titles match their scene labels, and l40 clearly separates two upgrades. At l38, retained outcome captions compete with the new headline.

P4.evidence: l15 “How big each step” sounds unfinished; cold-open l06 “How to find the bottom?” is an awkward question-heading construction.

P5.evidence: In s0_l04–s0_l07, “Per km ($)” becomes almost invisible against the faded map. Package-card layout and final subtitle interaction cannot be verified from the supplied images.

P6.evidence: Every issue below includes replacement wording, including “Step size,” “Valley in 3 steps,” and a shorter, structured outro.

P2.name: Divided from narration
P2.a_ev: Division of labour is mostly good (numbers, contrasts, labels on screen). Near-verbatim echoes: l24 "The floor: a long, gentle trench" vs narration "The floor is a long, gentle trench"; l47 "Turned one small step at a time" vs "one small step at a time"; l45 "Each knob gets its own step size" vs "gives each knob its own step size"; outro "Feel for the steepest way down" is l48 word for word. l04 "Billions: no map" understates "hundreds of billions of knobs".
P2.b_ev: l33–l39 add “Still halfway,” whereas narration says “still far from the bottom.” l45 and the outro repeat explanations already delivered aloud.
P2.judge_reason: b 站得住。严格项里有贴着口播的问题，按规则都算必改：outro 的 "Feel for the steepest way down" 与 l48 逐字相同（a 自己在证据里也写了），冷开场 l04 的 "Billions: no map" 和口播 "hundreds of billions of knobs" 对不上（zh 版写的是"几千亿个"）。另外 l33–l39 的 "Still halfway" 是口播没说过的量化判断（口播只说 "still far from the bottom"）；从 s4_l38 看路径终点只在几何上大约走了一半，按分数是从 78 降到 5.5，基本到了底，所以这个词会误导。l24、l45、l47 近乎逐字重复口播，两位都列了。a 列出了必改证据却给 2 分，前后矛盾。

P3.a_ev: Chapter numbering 01–04 and eyebrows are consistent, and ≤3 levels hold. P3.judge_reason: 两人都漏了章节标题的一致性。第 03 章 "How big a step?" 和第 04 章 "How big models train" 是相邻章，都以 "How big" 开头，意思却不同（前者问步子大小，后者的 big 修饰 models），l15 的 h1 "How big each step" 又是一个 "How big"。连着看，04 很容易被读成第三个"多大"的问题。这是严格项（章节标题），必改。a 指出了 l13/l15 术语只出现在小号 eyebrow、Upgrade ①② 与 01–04 编号体系冲突，这两条成立。
